source_text: ἀναπνέομεν. ἔλαθον τοίνυν ἑαυτοὺς ὡς δι' ὧν ἀκαίρως ἡμῖν οὐ συντίθενται καὶ εἰς τὸν ἀκατάσειστον οἶκον ἐπάνεισιν τὸν ἐν ἀρχαῖς. ὅθεν ἀπεπήδησαν, πράγματα πλέκουσι τῷ ἀποστόλῳ, αὐτῶν ἕνεκα διαμαρτυραμένῳ ἐν τοῖς ἐγκειμένοις αὐτοῦ ῥήμασιν ἐνώπιον τῆς ἀκτίστου φύσεως καὶ τῆς κτιστῆς, παραπλησίως πως τοῦ εἰπόντος· «ἥμαρτον τῷ θεῷ καὶ ἀνθρώποις,» καί· «διαμαρτύρομαι σήμερον τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν,» καί· «ἄκουε, οὐρανέ, καὶ ἐνωτίζου, γῆ.» 6.20ν ὅτι κοινωνεῖ, ὡς τῇ οὐσίᾳ, οὕτως καὶ τοῖς ὀνόμασιν, τῷ θεῷ πνεύματι καὶ τῷ μονογενεῖ αὐτοῦ υἱῷ ἡ κτίσις ἀκοινώτητα ἔχει τὰ ὀνόματα πρὸς τὰ ἐπὶ τοῦ θεοῦ λεγόμενα ὀνόματα, ὡς καὶ τὴν φύσιν. τὸ δὲ ἅγιον πνεῦμα κοινωνεῖ τοῖς ὀνόμασι τοῦ θεοῦ διὰ τὸ καὶ τῇ φύσει κοινωνεῖν, πλὴν ὅτι ὁ πατὴρ μόνος καλεῖται «πατήρ», διὰ τὸ μόνον ὑποστάσει γεννῆσαι, καὶ ὁ υἱὸς «υἱὸς» καὶ οὐ πατὴρ ἀκτίστου φύσεως, διὰ τὸ ἀληθῶς γεννηθῆναι μέν, μὴ γεννῆσαι δέ. ὡς ἡνίκα ἡ γραφὴ ὀνομάζει καὶ αὐτὸ τὸ πνεῦμα «κύριον», ὡς πάντων δεσπόζον καὶ κοινωνοῦν τῆς μιᾶς βασιλείας τῷ πατρὶ καὶ τῷ υἱῷ· «ἅγιον», ὡς αὐτὸ φύσει ἅγιον καὶ ὡς τὴν κτίσιν ἁγιάζον· «ἄφθαρτον», «ἀγαθόν», «ἀγάπην», «σοφίαν», «σύνεσιν», ὡς καὶ τὸν θεὸν προσηγόρευσεν· «δύναμιν» ἀφ' ὧν ἐνδυναμοῖ· «δίκαιον», ἀφ' ὧν δικαιοῖ, αὐτοαναμάρτητον ὑπάρχον· «παράκλητον», ὡς καὶ τὸν υἱόν· «πῦρ», ἀφ' ὧν ὤφθη τοῖς ἀποστόλοις πυρίναις γλώσσαις, καθὰ περὶ μὲν τοῦ πατρὸς λέγει Μωυσῆς· «ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν πῦρ καταναλίσκον,» περὶ δὲ τοῦ υἱοῦ Ἰωάννης· «αὐτὸς ὑμᾶς βαπτίσει ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ καὶ πυρί,» καὶ ὅσα τοιαῦτα. 6.21ν ὅτι ἕν ἐστιν καὶ οὐ πολλά, ὡς τὰ κτίσματα. ἡ κτίσις οὐδὲν ἔχει ἐν μιᾷ ὑποστάσει ἤτοι ἐν ἑνὶ προσώπῳ ὑπάρχον. καὶ γὰρ ἄγγελοι καὶ ἀρχάγγελοι πολλοί, τὰ σεραφὶμ ὁμοίως, τὰ χερουβὶμ οὐχ ἕν τί ἐστιν, ἀρχαὶ καὶ ἐξουσίαι εἴρηνται, δυνάμεις καὶ κυριότητες καὶ θρόνοι· πληθυντικῶς οὐρανοί, ἄνθρωποι καὶ τὰ λοιπὰ ποιήματα. κοινωνεῖ γὰρ καὶ ἥλιος καὶ σελήνη τῷ πλήθει τῶν ἄστρων τῇ τε φύσει καὶ τῷ πυροειδεῖ, ὡς ἐξεργαστικώτερον ὁ πρῶτος τοῦτο 66 περιέσχεν λόγος. τὸ δὲ ἅγιον πνεῦμα, ὡς μὴ ἐναρίθμιον τῇ κτίσει, ἓν καὶ τὸ αὐτὸ εἶναι τὰ λόγια ἡμῖν προσανεφώνησεν. 6.22ν ὅτι διὰ τὸ ὁμοούσιον καὶ ἄναρχον γέγραπται εἶναι ὕδωρ ζωῆς ἐκ τῆς πατρικῆς πηγῆς ἐκπορευθέν. ἡ κτίσις οὐ γέγραπται εἶναι ὕδωρ ζωῆς· οὐ γὰρ ἀφ' ἑαυτῆς ἔσχεν ἀειζωίαν, ὡς ὁ ἀνάρχως ζῶν θεός. τὸ δὲ ἅγιον πνεῦμα τοῦτο εἶναι εὐφημοῦσιν οἱ ἐν τοῖς ὑπογεγραμμένοις μνημονευθησόμενοι ἱεροκήρυκες, ὡς ἐκ τῆς ἀθανάτου καὶ φυσιζώου πατρικῆς πηγῆς συμφυῶς ἐκπορευόμενον, οὐχὶ κτιζόμενον. καθάπερ γὰρ ἐν τῷ πρώτῳ εἴπομεν λόγῳ, ὅτι τὸ φῶς οὐ γενεσιουργεῖ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ αὐγήν, ἀλλὰ γεννᾷ, οὕτως ἐνταῦθα, ὅτι ἡ πηγὴ οὐ γενεσιουργεῖ τὸ ἐξ αὐτῆς ὕδωρ, ἀλλ' ἐκπορευόμενον ἔχει καὶ ὁμοούσιον οὐδεὶς γὰρ τοῦ ἑαυτοῦ ἢ υἱοῦ ἢ πνεύματος γενεσιουργός ἐστιν· ἐπεὶ οὐκέτι πατήρ, οὔτε πνεῦμα ἔχων. Ἰερεμίας ἐκ προσώπου τοῦ θεοῦ· «ἐξέστη ὁ οὐρανὸς ἐπὶ τούτῳ, καὶ ἔφριξεν ἐπὶ τούτῳ ἡ γῆ· ὅτι δύο καὶ πονηρὰ ἐποίησεν ὁ λαός μου. ἐμὲ ἐγκατέλιπον πηγὴν ὕδα τος ζῶντος, καὶ ὤρυξαν ἑαυτοῖς λάκκους συντετριμμένους, οἳ οὐ δυνήσονται ὕδωρ συνέχειν.» τὸ μυστήριον ὁ προφήτης μυστηρικῶς ἐκτίθεται. εἶπεν γὰρ «πηγὴν» τὸν θεόν, «ὕδωρ» δὲ «ζῶν» τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα, τὸ ἐν τῇ κολυμβήθρᾳ πάσας ἡμῶν ἐκκαθαῖρον τὰς ἁμαρτίας, τὸ διασπασθῆναι τῇ φύσει τῆς νοητῆς πηγῆς μὴ δυνάμενον, ὡς καὶ τὸ ἐκ πηγῶν ῥεῖθρον. Ἠσαῖας ὁμοίως· «ἐγὼ δώσω ὕδωρ ἐν δίψῃ τοῖς πορευομένοις ἐν ἀνύδρῳ· ἐπιθήσω τὸ πνεῦμά μου ἐπὶ τὸ σπέρμα σου καὶ τὰς εὐλογίας μου ἐπὶ τὰ τέκνα σου· καὶ ἀνατελοῦσιν ἀνὰ μέσον ὕδατος ὡς χόρτος, καὶ ὡς ἰτέα ἐπὶ παραρρέον ὕδωρ.» καὶ τοῦτο διὰ κρυφίων ἔχει νοητὴν διαίρεσιν. τοῖς γὰρ ἐν ἀγνοίᾳ, φησίν, τυγχάνουσιν τοῦ βαπτίσματος καὶ διὰ τοῦτο «πορευομένοις ἐν ἀνύδρῳ» «ἐπιθήσω τὸ πνεῦμά μου» τὸ ποιῆσαι δυνάμενον τὴν κολυμβήθραν ἀναθῆλαι αὐτοὺς ὡς τὰ φίλυδρα τῶν φυτῶν, καὶ· «ὡς τὸ ξύλον τὸ πεφυτευμένον παρὰ τὰς διεξόδους τῶν ὑδάτων· ὃ τὸν καρπὸν αὐτοῦ δώσει ἐν καιρῷ αὐτοῦ, καὶ τὸ φύλλον αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἀπορρυήσεται.» καὶ ὁ ἱεροψάλτης τὸ ἀληθὲς τῷ πράγματι ἀφανές πως τῷ λόγῳ διὰ τὸ ἀναγκαῖον ποιῶν ἀναμέλπει ἐν μὲν λεʹ ψαλμῷ· «ὅτι παρὰ σοὶ πηγὴ ζωῆς,» ἐν δὲ ρμζʹ· «ἐξαποστελεῖ τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ καὶ τήξει αὐτά· πνεύσει τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ῥυήσεται ὕδατα εὐφραίνοντα τὴν πόλιν τοῦ θεοῦ τὴν μεγάλην·» αὕτη δέ ἐστιν ἡ πᾶσα οἰκουμένη. ἵνα οὕτως γὰρ εἴπω, ὅπερ ἀνθρώποις ἐστὶν ἑκάστη πόλις, τοῦτο παντοκράτορι ἡ
pass_a_gloss: [Continuing from the previous section: ... as for us that which] we breathe. So they have escaped their own notice, how through the things in which they unseasonably do not agree with us they are going back into the unshaken house of the beginnings, from which they leapt away. They weave troubles for the apostle, who on their account solemnly testified in his words lying before us before the uncreated nature and the created, somewhat like the one who said: 'I sinned against God and men,' and: 'I solemnly call to witness today the heaven and the earth,' and: 'hear, heaven, and give ear, earth.' 6.20ν [Chapter title:] That it shares, as in the substance, so also in the names, with God who is Spirit and with his only-begotten Son. The creation has the names unshared with the names said of God, as also the nature. But the Holy Spirit shares in the names of God because it also shares in the nature, except that the Father alone is called 'Father', because he alone begot in hypostasis, and the Son 'Son' and not father of an uncreated nature, because he was truly begotten but did not beget. As when the Scripture names the Spirit itself also 'Lord', as ruling over all and sharing in the one kingdom with the Father and the Son; 'holy', as itself holy by nature and as sanctifying the creation; 'incorruptible', 'good', 'love', 'wisdom', 'understanding', as it also addressed God; 'power', from the things by which it empowers; 'righteous', from the things by which it makes righteous, being itself without sin; 'Paraclete', as also the Son; 'fire', from the things by which it was seen by the apostles in fiery tongues, as about the Father Moses says: 'our God is a consuming fire,' and about the Son John: 'he will baptize you in Holy Spirit and fire,' and as many such things. 6.21ν [Chapter title:] That it is one and not many, as the creatures. The creation has nothing existing in one hypostasis, that is, in one person. For both angels and archangels are many, the Seraphim likewise, the Cherubim are not some one thing, principalities and authorities have been spoken of, powers and dominions and thrones; in the plural heavens, men and the remaining things made. For both sun and moon share with the multitude of the stars both in the nature and in the fiery form, as the first book [page number 66, debris] encompassed this more elaborately. But the Holy Spirit, as not numbered with the creation, the oracles proclaimed to us to be one and the same. 6.22ν [Chapter title:] That because of the consubstantial and beginningless it is written to be water of life proceeded from the paternal fountain. The creation is not written to be water of life; for it did not have everlasting life from itself, as the beginninglessly living God. But the Holy Spirit to be this the sacred heralds who will be mentioned in the things written below speak well of, as proceeding connaturally from the immortal and naturally living paternal fountain, not being created. For just as in the first book we said that the light does not bring into being its own radiance, but begets it, so here, that the fountain does not bring into being the water from it, but has it proceeding and consubstantial; for no one is the bringer-into-being of his own either son or spirit; since then no longer father, nor having a spirit. Jeremiah from the person of God: 'heaven was astonished at this, and the earth shuddered at this; for two and evil things my people did. Me they abandoned, fountain of living water, and dug for themselves broken cisterns, which will not be able to hold water.' The prophet sets out the mystery mystically. For he said 'fountain' for God, and 'living water' for the Holy Spirit, the one in the font cleansing out all our sins, the one not able to be torn away by nature from the intelligible fountain, as also the stream from springs. Isaiah likewise: 'I will give water in thirst to those walking in a waterless place; I will place my Spirit upon your seed and my blessings upon your children; and they will spring up in the midst of water as grass, and as a willow by running-past water.' And this through hidden things has an intelligible distinction. For to those, he says, being in ignorance of baptism and through this 'walking in a waterless place' 'I will place my Spirit', the one able to make the font make them bloom again like the water-loving of the plants, and: 'as the tree planted by the outlets of the waters, which will give its fruit in its season, and its leaf will not fall off.' And the sacred psalmist, making the truth in the matter somewhat unseen in the word through necessity, sings in the 35th psalm (LXX; English 36): 'for with you is the fountain of life,' and in the 147th: 'he will send out his word and melt them; he will blow his Spirit, and waters will flow gladdening the great city of God;' and this is the whole inhabited world. pass_b_english: …we breathe. So, without noticing it, by the very arguments in which they so untimely refuse to agree with us, they are going back into the unshaken house of the beginning, from which they leapt away. They make trouble for the Apostle, who on their account, in the words of his now before us, solemnly testified before the uncreated nature and the created, much as the one who said, “I have sinned against God and against men,” and “I call heaven and earth to witness this day” (Deuteronomy 4:26; Deuteronomy 30:19), and “Hear, O heaven, and give ear, O earth” (Isaiah 1:2).
That he shares with God, who is Spirit, and with his only-begotten Son, in the names as in the substance.

Creation has names that are not shared with the names spoken of God, just as it has a nature that is not shared. But the Holy Spirit shares in the names of God because he shares in the nature too; except that the Father alone is called “Father,” because he alone begot a hypostasis, and the Son is called “Son,” and not father of an uncreated nature, because he was truly begotten but did not beget. So Scripture names the Spirit himself as well “Lord,” as ruling over all and sharing the one kingdom with the Father and the Son; “Holy,” as holy by nature himself and as making creation holy; “Incorruptible,” “Good,” “Love,” “Wisdom,” “Understanding,” as it has also called God; “Power,” because he gives power; “Righteous,” because he makes righteous, being himself without sin; “Paraclete,” as it calls the Son too; “Fire,” because he appeared to the apostles in tongues of fire (Acts 2:3). In the same way Moses says of the Father, “Our God is a consuming fire” (Deuteronomy 4:24), and John says of the Son, “He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire” (Matthew 3:11); and there are many more such names.
That he is one and not many, as creatures are.

Creation has nothing that exists in a single hypostasis, that is, in one person. For angels and archangels are many; so are the Seraphim; the Cherubim are not some single thing; principalities and authorities are spoken of, powers and dominions and thrones; the heavens are named in the plural, and so are men and the rest of the things that were made. Even sun and moon share with the multitude of the stars both in nature and in being of fire, as the first book set out more fully. But the oracles have proclaimed to us that the Holy Spirit, as not to be counted among creation, is one and the same.
That because he is consubstantial and without beginning, he is written to be the water of life, which has proceeded from the Father’s fountain.

Creation is not written to be the water of life, for it did not have everlasting life from itself, as God has, who lives without beginning. But the Holy Spirit is praised as being this by the sacred heralds who will be mentioned in what is written below, as proceeding by nature from the immortal and naturally living fountain of the Father, not as being created. For just as we said in the first book that light does not create its own radiance but begets it, so here we say that the fountain does not create the water that comes from it, but has it proceeding from itself and consubstantial with itself. For no one is the creator of his own son or spirit; otherwise he would no longer be father, nor one who has a spirit.

Jeremiah, speaking in the person of God: “Heaven was astonished at this, and the earth shuddered at this; for my people have done two evil things. They have forsaken me, the fountain of living water, and dug for themselves broken cisterns, which will not be able to hold water” (Jeremiah 2:12-13). The prophet sets out the mystery in a hidden way. For he called God “fountain,” and the Holy Spirit “living water”: the Spirit who in the font washes away all our sins, who cannot be torn away from the nature of the spiritual fountain, as neither can the stream that flows from springs.

Isaiah likewise: “I will give water in thirst to those who walk in a waterless land; I will put my Spirit upon your seed and my blessings upon your children; and they shall spring up in the midst of water like grass, and like a willow beside running water” (Isaiah 44:3-4). This too, through hidden words, has a spiritual sense. For to those, he says, who are ignorant of baptism, and for that reason “walk in a waterless land,” “I will put my Spirit,” who is able to make the font bring them to flower again like plants that love water, and “like the tree planted by the channels of the waters, which will give its fruit in its season, and its leaf will not fall” (Psalm 1:3).

And the sacred psalmist, out of necessity making the truth of the matter somewhat hidden in his words, sings in the thirty-sixth Psalm, “For with you is the fountain of life” (Psalm 36:9), and in the hundred and forty-seventh, “He will send out his word and melt them; he will blow with his Spirit, and waters will flow” (Psalm 147:18), “making glad the great city of God” (Psalm 46:4). choices.issue: Garbled draft, chapter titles run together, references
choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-e-u16): retranslated. The old English made nonsense of the opening ('they hid themselves as through whom we are unseasonably not being gathered together'), read ἀκτίστου as 'created', αὐτοαναμάρτητον as 'self-righteous', ἐξέστη as 'were out of joint', and the Isaiah 44 exposition as 'those in ignorance happen to receive the baptism' and 'make the baptismal pool overflow'. The 6.22 chapter title was split across two paragraphs. References: (Jeremiah 2:12) -> 2:12-13; (Isaiah 44:3) -> 44:3-4; (Psalm 147:18) kept and (Psalm 46:4) added for 'making glad the city of God'; new references checked against the KJV text.

choices.why: The section opens mid-sentence (previous section: ὡς ἡμῖν ὃ, 'just as with us that which'); only the words this section holds are translated.

choices.term: ἔλαθον τοίνυν ἑαυτοὺς ... ἐπάνεισιν ... ὅθεν ἀπεπήδησαν
choices.english: without noticing it ... they are going back into the unshaken house of the beginning, from which they leapt away
choices.why: ἐπάνεισιν is read with the Macedonians as subject (their own arguments lead them back to the faith they left); ὅθεν ἀπεπήδησαν is taken with the 'house', though the copy-text punctuates before it. Recorded in problems.

choices.term: ἐνώπιον τῆς ἀκτίστου φύσεως καὶ τῆς κτιστῆς
choices.english: before the uncreated nature and the created
choices.why: Didymus' answer to the Macedonian use of 1 Timothy 5:21: God and Christ are the uncreated witnesses, the elect angels the created ones, as heaven and earth are called to witness in Deuteronomy and Isaiah.
The dative noun stands in apposition to God (compare John 4:24); a reading 'the Spirit [shares] with God' would need a nominative. Recorded in problems.

choices.english: because he alone begot a hypostasis
choices.why: The Father alone begets a real, subsisting Son; the dative ὑποστάσει is taken as the thing begotten in its own subsistence.

choices.term: ἀφ' ὧν ἐνδυναμοῖ / ἀφ' ὧν δικαιοῖ
choices.english: because he gives power / because he makes righteous
choices.why: The names are drawn from what the Spirit does; 'from which' is turned into a causal clause.
λόγος here is a book of the treatise, as ἐν τῷ πρώτῳ εἴρηται βιβλίῳ in the previous section.
An interpretation that the mind discerns beneath the letter; 'intellectual division' was a crib.

choices.term: τὸ ἀληθὲς τῷ πράγματι ἀφανές πως τῷ λόγῳ διὰ τὸ ἀναγκαῖον ποιῶν
choices.english: out of necessity making the truth of the matter somewhat hidden in his words
choices.why: The psalmist veils the truth in figures; the old English said the opposite ('to make the truth apparent').

choices.term: ἐν μὲν λεʹ ψαλμῷ ... ἐν δὲ ρμζʹ
choices.english: in the thirty-sixth Psalm ... in the hundred and forty-seventh
choices.why: Greek Psalm 35 = English 36 (verse 10 = 36:9); Greek Psalm 147 = English 147:12-20 (verse 7 = 147:18), so the English number stays 147.

choices.term: ῥυήσεται ὕδατα εὐφραίνοντα τὴν πόλιν τοῦ θεοῦ τὴν μεγάλην
choices.english: waters will flow (Psalm 147:18), “making glad the great city of God” (Psalm 46:4)
choices.why: Didymus runs Psalm 147:18 into Psalm 46:4 (and the 'great' city of Psalm 48:2); the quotation is split so each reference matches its words.

choices.english: as the first book set out more fully
choices.why: 66 is a printed page number in the copy-text, skipped. 'ὕδα τος' is a line-break split of ὕδατος.
